name: Thomas Aquinas and the Summa Theologiae
summary: Thomas Aquinas, a Dominican friar at the University of Paris, writes the Summa Theologiae (1265-1274), the comprehensive synthesis of Aristotelian philosophy and Christian theology. The unfinished work systematizes Christian doctrine through the Scholastic method of objection, counter-argument, and resolution. Aquinas's natural law theory, that reason can discern moral principles independently of revelation, becomes the foundation of Catholic social and political thought.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Summa Theologiae is the intellectual achievement of medieval Christendom; Aquinas's synthesis shapes Catholic theology, philosophy of law, and political theory for centuries; his argument that reason and faith are complementary (not opposed) legitimizes the study of Aristotle and creates the philosophical framework that enables early modern science; 'Thomism' becomes the official philosophy of the Catholic Church (confirmed in 1879)
